---
title: "05 · Plots"
engine: er2
format: html
---

Figures come from Matplotlib, imported as in any Python program. Every
figure still open at the end of a cell is saved — SVG for HTML, PDF for
LaTeX, PNG otherwise — and shown. Matplotlib must be installed in the
environment ER2 runs in.

## A labelled figure

A `fig-` label and a caption make a numbered figure that can be
cross-referenced:

```{er2}
#| label: fig-primepi
#| fig-cap: "The prime-counting function $\\pi(x)$ against $x / \\log x$."
#| fig-alt: "A staircase rising above a smooth curve."
import math
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

xs = list(range(2, 1001))
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3.5))
plt.step(xs, [primepi(n) for n in xs], where="post", label="primepi(x)")
plt.plot(xs, [n / math.log(n) for n in xs], label="x / log x")
plt.legend()
```

@fig-primepi shows that $x/\log x$ undercounts the primes: at $x = 1000$
it gives about 145, while $\pi(1000) =$ `{er2} primepi(1000)`.

## ER2 values in a plot

ER2 numbers are Python numbers, so they go straight into Matplotlib; and
`latex()` returns a string, so it can be a label.

```{er2}
#| label: fig-phi
#| fig-cap: "Euler's totient."
ns = range(1, 201)
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3.5))
plt.scatter(ns, [phi(n) for n in ns], s=4)
plt.title(r"$\varphi(n)$")
plt.xlabel("$n$");
```

## Several figures in one cell

Each open figure is saved in turn; only the first can take the label.

```{er2}
#| echo: false
for k in (2, 3):
    plt.figure(figsize=(3, 2))
    plt.plot([n^k for n in range(10)])
    plt.title(f"$n^{k}$")
```
